text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.8% today, extending a steep two-week decline that has wiped out roughly 7% of the stock's value. The immediate driver is a sharp drop in oil prices following diplomatic talks between the U.S. and Iran at the UN—investors are betting that an easing of Middle East tensions and a potential reopening of the Strait of Hormuz would increase global oil supply, putting downward pressure on crude prices. With US oil trading around $107 per barrel (down from levels that were much higher just two weeks ago), refiners and oil producers face lower revenues per barrel, and ConocoPhillips is caught in that pullback.

The bigger picture is that oil markets have shifted on de-escalation hopes. When geopolitical risk premiums disappear—meaning traders no longer add extra money to prices just because of conflict risk—commodity prices tend to fall, and energy stocks follow. The gap between global oil ($130.80) and US oil ($107.02) also hints at supply concerns being priced out, which typically benefits buyers but hurts producers holding inventory at lower realized prices.
